common.envelopeLayout: 0x01 || nonce(12) || BE64(seq) || BE16(ctLen) || ct ; ct = AES-256-GCM(key, nonce, no AAD, paddedBlock) = 272 bytes
common.innerPlaintextNote: 40 bytes, b[i] = (3*i + 1) mod 256. Padded block = BE16(40) || body || tail, 256 bytes, tail[i] = (7*i + 13) mod 256 for i = 0.. (production tails are random).
common.outerKeyDerivation: HKDF-SHA256(IKM = sessionKey, salt = "qaudion-srtp-salt-v1", info = "q-audion-srtp-master-v1:" + callId + ":a2b"|":b2a", L = 32)
common.outerLayout: nonce(12) || AES-256-GCM(key, nonce, no AAD, plaintext) ; the counter is nonce bytes 4..11, first counter is 0

counterAcrossRekeyRevert.asserted: all nonces of the sequence are pairwise distinct; ctr increases by one at each seal across rekey, revert, profile latch and leg swap

fullChain.note: inner envelope above sealed by the legacy outer layer of the caller (role A: key outerKeyA2B, nonce prefix dirTag o2a = 0x01, outer counter 0)

innerNonceV1.rule: N = dirTag(self) || 0x00 0x00 0x00 || BE64(ctr_in); ctr_in starts at 1, is incremented before each seal, never reset

legacyOuterNonce.distinctNonceProperty: two senders under the same key and the same counter (a tie, same key) differ in byte 0 when one is caller and one callee
legacyOuterNonce.rule: current sender: byte 0 = dirTag by R-ROLE (0x01 caller, 0x02 callee), bytes 1..3 = 0, bytes 4..11 = BE64(counter). Old sender: bytes 0..3 = 0.

level.groupRule: H = own tl pq and every other member announced tl pq; K = same for kd; PQ2 if H and K, PQ1 if exactly one, CL if none; a member that announces nothing makes both facts false and counts once in unk. A member that announces only one of tl/kd is not covered by a vector (the spec does not define unk for it).
level.layerRule: A path's PQ layers, each tagged with its secret: dtls (DTLS hop, only when group = pq); session (FrameCryptor of rtp, the inner layer of dcmux/relay/rvideo when inner = pq, and a 'same' outer layer); relaySS (an 'ind' or 'indrot' outer layer). Path level: 2+ distinct secrets -> PQ2; 2+ layers sharing one secret -> PQ2S; one layer -> PQ1; none -> CL.

logLine.note: single line, tokens separated by one space, in the order of section 6.4; an empty value prints as '-'; the group tokens tl, kd and unk follow only when kind=group

level.rank: CL < PQ1 < PQ2S < PQ2; the level of a call is the weakest of its used paths

mldsaSeed.derivation: xi = HKDF-SHA256(IKM = edSeed, salt = "qaudion-mldsa87-seed-v1", info = "qaudion-identity-mldsa87" || edPub[32] || BE16(gen), L = 32); mldsaPub = FIPS 204 ML-DSA-87 KeyGen_internal(xi)
mldsaSeed.edSeedNote: seedN = SHA-256("pqc-hardening-v1/kat/edSeed/N"); case rfc8032-test1-gen0 uses the RFC 8032 section 7.1 test 1 secret key

negatives.name: expanded-scalar-as-seed
negatives.why: RFC 8032 public key derived from the stored bytes differs from the published key

negatives.name: public-key-of-another-identity
negatives.why: published key does not match the seed

mldsaSeed.rfc8032Check: edPub is derived from edSeed with RFC 8032 and compared with the published key before deriving xi; a mismatch is refused (negatives)
mldsaSeed.settlesQ4: every platform stores or can reproduce the 32-byte RFC 8032 seed; the vectors fix the derivation from that seed

nackResend.direction: caller to callee (o2a), outer key outerKeyA2B, prefix 0x01; frame i uses body b[j] = (3*j + 1 + seq) mod 256

events.reason: entry of round 1 dropped at the send switch

nackResend.eventsNote: frames 1..3 are sent in round 1 (outer counters 0..2); events 1-2 happen before the send switch; frame 4 is sent after the switch (inner seq continues, outer counter 3).

forbiddenReseal.note: re-sealing the cached inner envelope of frame 1 through the outer sealer (old Android behaviour) consumes a new outer counter and yields different bytes; a conforming sender never does it

nackResend.layers: legacy inner (sessionKey of the round, B1 nonce, plaintext opusStandIn(40, seq)) + legacy outer (round-1 keys, never rotated)
nackResend.rule: the cache stores the final wire bytes after every layer; a resend sends them unchanged and calls no sealer; the cache is zero-filled and dropped when the send switch moves to a new round

outerOffV1.classification: checked before the outer open: exactly the two bytes 0x03 0x03 on the DC-mux leg -> honour; the same bytes on the relay leg -> ignore (dropped); anything else -> normal path (outer open)
outerOffV1.honourEffects: rule 3 for the call: stop the outer seal on the DC-mux leg, disarm the relay leg, accept inner-sealed frames unwrapped on the DC-mux leg only
outerOffV1.layout: control mux byte 0x03 || kind 0x03, empty body; kinds: hangup 0x01, NACK request 0x02, outer-off-v1 0x03
outerOffV1.sendSide: DC-mux leg only, never through the outer sealer or the relay; repeated with the first three inner-sealed frames

phase: 1 (steps S0-S7, no wire change) + S13 vectors (mldsaSeed, xcert, sigHybrid; no wire change)

roleTie.note: Keys are the legacy outer keys of common; role A sends with outerKeyA2B and opens outerKeyB2A, role B the opposite. The last scenario (both A) cannot open each other's frames: the documented denial; the nonces still differ in byte 0. Frames are outer counter 0.
roleTie.rule: tie iff lowercased user ids are equal; non-tie: role A iff the lowercased byte string of self sorts before peer (a prefix sorts first, equal counts as A). Tie: table of B7.2 change 2. Ids in the vectors are ASCII.

tieScenarios.name: caller advertises capsBindV1, callee (old build) does not
caller does not advertise, callee does

inputs.note: bundle hashes, fingerprints and EXTX are SHA-256 of fixed labels (fingerprints with a leading 0x01); CAPSX is an arbitrary fixed byte string here, its internal format belongs to section capsx

keys.note: the ML-DSA public key is mldsaSeed.cases[0].mldsaPub

sigHybrid.layoutHT: HT = "qaudion-hs-hybrid-v1"(20) || u8(kind) || SHA-256(T)[32] || edPub[32] || mldsaKeyId[32] || DTLSFP_self[33] || (ACCEPT only) DTLSFP_peer[33] || BE16(len(CAPSX)) || CAPSX || EXTX[32]; kind OFFER 0x01, ACCEPT 0x02

pins.createdMs: the bundle field mldsa_xc_created_ms (not created_at_ms), decimal string
pins.deviceId: the exact UTF-8 bytes as registered; non-empty, at most 255 bytes, valid UTF-8, no Unicode normalization (nfc-device-id and nfd-device-id are different byte strings)
pins.keysFromCase: seedCase indexes mldsaSeed.cases; the ML-DSA public key of a vector is that case's mldsaPub
pins.uuid_raw: the account UUID as 16 bytes in RFC 4122 network byte order (internal/sigsum ComputeLeaf, uuid16)

xcert.xcPq: ML-DSA-87 pure mode over XC with FIPS 204 context "qaudion-identity-xcert-v1", 4627 bytes; the vector uses deterministic signing (rnd = 0^32), production signing is hedged
